name: Desmodium styracifolium
short: Data are for a total-flavonoid extract in ureteral-stone patients: in a 606-person trial adverse events were similar to placebo (19.3% vs 18.2%); one cohort reported no adverse reactions.
text: The safety data found are for an extract of the total flavonoids (flavones) of Desmodium styracifolium (taken by mouth as capsules in the phase 3 trial; the cohort study's abstract does not give the form or route), not for the whole herb or its teas. In a phase 3 double-blind randomised trial in 606 adults with ureteral stones, who also took investigator-prescribed background medication, adverse event rates were similar with the extract and with placebo (19.3% versus 18.2%); the abstract does not list the adverse events or say whether any were serious. A retrospective cohort study of 341 outpatients with ureteral stones, in which the extract was used alongside medical expulsive therapy, reported no adverse drug reactions, and its authors concluded the extract appears to be a safe adjunct. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
